blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At enterprise scale, data protection is a programme, not a document. Every country where the company operates brings its own regulator, its own language, its own deadlines, and sometimes its own philosophy about what privacy actually means. The senior leader's task is to turn this complicated patchwork into something coherent enough that the team can live with it — and honest enough that the auditors believe it.

The central idea is a single data map: every dataset the company holds, its purpose, its legal basis, its retention rule, and its owner. Everything else — requests from individuals, responses to regulators, cross-border transfers — is built on top of that map. Without the map, the programme is a collection of guesses. With it, the programme has a spine.

Data protection is built quietly over years. It is never perfect, but it can be honest — and honest, at this level, is what matters most.

items.q: According to the text, at enterprise scale data protection is best understood as…
options: a single deadline shared across countries
a philosophy imposed by one regulator
a legal defence built for auditors
items.why: "data protection is a programme, not a document" — a frase de abertura da lição.

items.q: What is described as sitting at the centre of the whole programme?
options: A single data map of every dataset held
The individual requests from data subjects
The relationship with each national regulator
items.why: "The central idea is a single data map… Everything else is built on top of that map."

items.q: The text says the leader must make the programme coherent enough for the team AND honest enough for whom?
items.why: "coherent enough that the team can live with it — and honest enough that the auditors believe it."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Credibility with auditors depends on honesty, not perfection.
A polished policy document is enough to protect data at scale.
A programme without the data map rests on guesswork.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que proteção de dados é um programa contínuo, não um documento — logo, um documento sozinho não basta.

items.q: Calling the data map "a spine" suggests that…
options: it is the most fragile part of the programme
it is only relevant to the auditors
it must be rewritten in every emergency
it is the structure that holds everything else up
items.why: Inferência: coluna = estrutura de sustentação; sem ela o programa é "a collection of guesses".

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte descrevendo o trabalho de construir o mapa de dados. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, where we've landed is this. For years, the same personal data was being stored in eight different folders, one per jurisdiction, and none of them agreed with the others. The German file said one retention period; the Singapore file said another; and nobody could tell me which one was actually being applied.

What I've been asked to deliver is a single map — every dataset we hold, why we hold it, the legal basis, when it must be deleted, and who owns it. It sounds unglamorous, and it is. But once it's written down honestly, the individual requests and the regulator responses more or less answer themselves.

I want to be candid about one thing. This will not be finished by the audit in March. It cannot be. A map like this is built slowly, and if we rush it, it will simply be wrong in a more organised way. What I can promise the auditors is that nothing has been hidden — every gap we know about is marked on the map as a gap.

That honesty is the point. A tidy document that quietly overstates our position would be far more dangerous than an incomplete one that tells the truth.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What was the problem with how the data used to be stored?
options: It was held in eight uncoordinated folders that disagreed with each other
It was stored only in Germany and Singapore
It was kept entirely on paper
It had been deleted before the audit
items.why: "eight different folders, one per jurisdiction, and none of them agreed with the others."

items.q: What is Charlotte being asked to deliver?
options: A single map covering every dataset, its purpose, legal basis, deletion date and owner
A faster process for answering individuals
A merged folder for Germany and Singapore only
A new policy document for each country
items.why: "a single map — every dataset we hold, why we hold it, the legal basis, when it must be deleted, and who owns it."

items.q: What does Charlotte say will happen once the map is written honestly?
options: The regulators will stop asking questions
The individual requests and regulator responses will more or less answer themselves
The eight folders can be reused
items.why: "the individual requests and the regulator responses more or less answer themselves."

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by warning it would otherwise be "wrong in a more organised way"?
options: A rushed map would look tidy but still contain errors
The map should be organised by country
items.why: Inferência: apressar não corrige os erros — só os deixa arrumados, o que é mais perigoso.

items.q: Which best captures Charlotte's underlying priority?
options: Honesty about gaps over the appearance of completeness
Finishing before March at any cost
Impressing the auditors with a polished document
items.why: Inferência: ela diz que um documento arrumado que exagera a posição é mais perigoso do que um incompleto que diz a verdade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We inherited a patchwork of local rules, each written by a different team." A patchwork is…
options: an uneven mix of pieces that don't quite fit together
items.why: Patchwork = colcha de retalhos: um conjunto irregular de partes que não combinam bem.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The framework must be ___ enough that the whole team applies it the same way."
items.why: Coherent = coerente: consistente o bastante para ser aplicado de modo uniforme.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Sending customer records from the EU to the US office counts as a ___."
items.why: Cross-border transfer = transferência transfronteiriça de dados entre jurisdições.

items.q: "Each dataset has a retention rule." This is…
options: the policy stating how long the data may be kept
the person responsible for the data
the legal basis for collecting it
the country where it is stored
items.why: Retention rule = regra de retenção: por quanto tempo o dado pode ser guardado antes de ser apagado.

items.q: "Without the map, the programme is just a set of guesses." Here, guesses means…
items.why: Guess = palpite: uma suposição sem base sólida — o oposto de um mapa documentado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em reuniões sobre compliance e proteção de dados. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal still has to sign off on the retention schedule." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the data map jurisdiction by jurisdiction." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "Two country teams pushed back on the shared deletion timeline." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed to fix the gaps but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Marking every known gap honestly is what will hold up under audit." To hold up here means to…
items.why: Hold up (under audit/scrutiny) = resistir ao exame, manter-se credível quando é testado.
